newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Southeast Asia stocks flounder on currency woes.
newsitem.headline: Southeast Asia stocks flounder on currency woes.

text.p: Southeast Asian stocks were sold down in July as currencies in the region suffered record lows on the heels of the Thai baht devaluation, Morgan Stanley Asia said in a monthly report issued on Tuesday.
Of the 49 markets covered by the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) indices, the Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia performed the worst, it said.
"Currency weakness was the driving force behind the market drops as the central banks took measures, including higher interest rates, to defend their currencies."
It said that while all three markets were hurt by currency weakness, internal factors were also at work.
The Philippine central bank raised bank reserve requirements by a percentage point, squeezing liquidity in the market.
Indonesian companies are expected to report poor first half earnings while Malaysian investors are negative on the economy's prospects, in particular the telecom sector's future growth.
Singapore's stock market ranked among the bottom performing developed markets in July, contracting by 2.7 percent.
The report said that after a mid-month rally in Singapore, investors took profits in the last week of July and turned their attention towards the buoyant Hong Kong market.
Hong Kong, which rose six percent, recorded the only positive performance in the Far East.
The MSCI Far East index fell 2.6 percent while its Europe index rose 4.5 percent, revealing a divergent performance between Europe and the Far East for the month of July, it said.
